443518.title: Bourdain, Anthony
443518.description:
Born June 25, 1956, in New York city, Anthony Bourdain's love of food came from his family visits to France in his youth. He spent years cooking, perhaps best known as executive chef at Brasserie Les Halles in New York. He rapidly rose to fame after his book "Kitchen Confidential" was released. It's an auto-biography that also tells the public what goes on behind the scenes in many restaurant kitchens. He was host of several food-related travel shows. He encouraged viewers to travel to unfamiliar places and eat unfamiliar foods, thus educating us, enriching our lives, eliminating racism and building understanding of other cultures.

While filming in Alsace, France, on June 8, 2018, he was found dead in his hotel room, apparently from suicide. He is survived by his daughter Ariane, born in 2007, and two ex-wives.

This area is for the listing of sites discussing sole or having recipes including it.

Sole - a species of thin, flat fish that swim on one side, have a small mouth, small or rudimentary fins, and small eyes placed close together and including superior food fishes such as the European Dover sole.

The following are not true sole fish:
Alaskan Plaice, American Plaice, English Sole, Lemon Sole, Pacific Dover Sole, Petrale Sole, Rex Sole, Rock Sole, and Yellowfin Sole – all are actually Flounder.

links.title: Sole Almondine
links.description: Uses 1 pound sole, slivered almonds, lemon juice, and optional white white. Makes 4 servings. From Taste of Home, which has member-submitted recipes that are reviewed in a test kitchen, and are rated by members.

links.title: Sole Meunière
links.description: Rated easy. Serves 4. A very traditional and popular preparation. Uses 4 4-ounce skinless sole or flounder fillets coated in instant flour, cooked in hot oil, then removed from heat, cooked briefly in butter and fresh lemon juice, and sprinkled with parsley. From Food Network Magazine.

links.title: Crab-stuffed Sole
links.description: Claims to be a Low-carb Keto recipe. Curlie editors do not test or verify these claims. Uses 1.5 lbs. sole, canned crab, cream cheese, mayonnaise, Tabasco, chives, and egg. Lay fish fillets flat, place other ingredients on top, roll up fillets, and bake.

443074.title: Tilapia
443074.description: Tilapia - Any of various cichlid fishes of the genus Tilapia, native to Africa but introduced elsewhere as a valuable food fish.

links.title: Tilapia Recipes
links.description: Offers several recipes including Blackened Tilapia, Tilapia In Beer Batter, and Tilapia Parmesan Saute.

links.title: Ginger Soy Tilapia
links.description: The fish is baked underneath aluminum foil to keep the steam of the fish in, keeping it moist.

links.title: Food.com - Tilapia
links.description: Tilapia recipes in a directory from Genius Kitchen.

links.title: Tilapia Recipes
links.description: Recipe collection presented by the American Tilapia Association.

links.title: Raspberry Tilapia
links.description: Tilapia baked in a raspberry vinegar and honey sauce.

443062.title: Trout
443062.description: Trout - members of the family of fishes known as Salmonidae, which includes the salmon. They are typically found in colder streams and lakes of North America, Europe, and Asia. Many kinds migrate to sea, but all spawn in fresh water.

links.title: United States Trout Farmers Association
links.description: Handling and preparation tips, plus recipes sorted by course. Examples are trout dilly dip, English trout pie, trout amandine, Wisconsin trout chowder, and lemon sauce.

links.title: Fresh Fish Kitchen
links.description: Large selection from Clear Springs Foods, producer of sustainably farmed rainbow trout. Can be searched or sorted; allergy, dairy, or gluten-free, Paleo, or traditional cooking. Examples are: tacos with bacon-pineapple jam, spice-rubbed with honey glazed fennel, fillets with cherry salsa, Ca Nuong La Chuoi (cooked in banana leaves), and smoky trout eggs Benedict with avocado.

443093.title: Tuna
443093.description: Tuna - Game and food fishes which have streamlined bodies with two fins, and five or more finlets on the back. The body is very narrow in the tail region, and the tail is deeply forked.

links.title: Fishing Vessel St. Jude

links.title: Wild Pacific Albacore

443626.title: Fondue

links.title: Dilled Garbanzo Fondue

links.title: Cheese Fondue

links.title: Crockpot Cheese Fondue Dip from RecipeSource

links.title: Minced Lamb Fondue from RecipeSource

links.title: Welsh Fondue

443008.title: For Children
443008.description:
This category is for sites that pertain to food and recipes suitable for children of all ages.

Subcategories include toddlers, preschoolers, children helping in the kitchen and baby food.

The baby food section has two subsections, one for preparation and storage of baby food, also including food safety, the other one is for teething biscuits.

links.title: Hummie's Kids Page
links.description: Recipes divided by categories for snacks, cookies, pizzas, candies, Hallowe'en, and fun edible and non-edible stuff such as playclay.

links.title: Kid Friendly Margarita Punch

links.title: Favourite Children's Recipes
links.description: A small collection of recipes to please children, young and old.

links.title: Kids Health: Recipes
links.description: Recipes for breakfast, snacks, frozen snacks, drinks and baked treats.

links.title: Fruit Pizza from Zoom Cafe
links.description: Snack made from fresh flour tortillas, peanut butter, raisins, and apple.

links.title: Beef and Lamb New Zealand: Babies and Toddlers

links.title: Party Foods - Snacks
links.description: Suggestions for snacks, beverages, desserts and main dishes for children's parties.

links.title: Lunch to Go: Nobby Apple Cake

links.title: Eating Richly

links.title: IndiaParenting.com: Babyfood Recipes

links.title: Baby Food

443438.title: Pomegranates
443438.description:
Pomegranate (Punica granatum) is a fruit-bearing shrub. Popular in the Middle East for centuries, it has become known as a "super food" and grows in many countries.

Inside the fruit, which is red and about the size of an apple, the edible part that most people call seeds are actually arils. Arils cover the seed and encourage birds to eat them and spread seeds in wide area. The juice surrounding the seed has a wine-y sweet/tart flavor.

443415.title: Sea Vegetables
443415.description:
Sea vegetables are edible plants, primarily seaweeds, that grow in or near the ocean. They have been harvested and eaten in Asian countries and other coastal areas for centuries. They have naturally high concentrations of nutrients, particularly minerals.

Some sea vegetables are known by a variety of names:

    Hiziki - hijiki
    Irish moss - carrageen moss
    Kombu - kelp, konbu, oarweed, sea cabbage, sea tangle
    Nori - laver, purple laver, purple seaweed
    Samphire - glasswort, marsh samphire, passe-pierre, pousse-pied, pousse-pierre, rock samphire, salicornia, sea asparagus, sea bean, sea green bean, sea fennel, sea pickle
    Wakame - Alaria is often sold as wakame in the U.S.
Recipe substitutions:
    Arame - dulse, hiziki, kombu, wakame
    Dulse - arame, hiziki, sea lettuce, wakame
    Hiziki - arame, dulse
    Sea lettuce - dulse, wakame
    Wakame - alaria, arame, dulse, sea lettuce

443038.title: Hanukkah
443038.description:
Hanukkah is a Jewish holiday also known as the Festival of Lights, observed for eight days and nights. It is not considered a major holiday.

A candle holder for 9 candles, called a menorah, is used. One candle is used to light all the other candles. The first night, one candle is lit, the second night, two candles are lit, and so on.

A story of its origins is the miracle of oil. When the Maccabees (a group of warriors) went to re-dedicate a temple, the oil supply was nearly gone, but by a miracle, it lasted 8 days. Because of the holiday's relation to oil, most foods for this holiday are fried in oil. The most popular are latkes (potato pancakes) and sufganiyot (jelly doughnuts). In recent years, savory fillings have become popular for the doughnuts.

443795.title: Ratatouille
443795.description:
This dish originated in Provence, in the south of France. Traditionally it contains eggplant, zucchini, tomatoes, and onions, sauteed separately and then and stirred together, with garlic, parsley, and thyme. Bell peppers and mushrooms are frequent additions, along with the local herbs (rosemary, sage, oregano, marjoram, and savory.)

Modern variations may add other ingredients, roast or bake the vegetables, or even microwave them. Sometimes ratatouille is presented as a thick stew or even a soup. It is usually a vegan dish, but some recipes add chicken, meat, or seafood, and many suggest serving it with Parmesan cheese on top.

443467.title: Vegetarian
443467.description:
Traditional vegetarian recipes and cooking tips for foods and meals which consist of grains, pasta, beans, vegetables, fruit can be placed in this category. Recipes which include meat, poultry, fish, or shellfish are not generally considered to be vegetarian.

This Vegetarian category can also include recipes which include animal products such as eggs, milk, cheese, and honey, and the like. These are considered acceptable to some vegetarians and is an eating pattern often referred to as "ovo-lacto vegetarian." Refer to the Vegan subcategory for eating patterns which are strictly limited to vegetable products, and exclude not only meat, poultry, fish, but also eggs, milk and dairy products, and insect products such as honey. In some parts of the world this eating pattern is referred to as "vegetarian" or "strictly vegetarian".

443046.description: A weblog is more commonly known as a blog. It's usually set up like a diary, with daily or regularly dated entries. The topics can vary from day to day. Writers use keywords and other specialized methods that enable readers to search the site. For instance, if you remember seeing a vanilla cupcake recipe with special birthday decorations, you don't have to memorize the date it was written to find it; you can use their search and look for "vanilla cupcake" or "birthday" or other combinations of those words, which are called keywords.

Periodic cicadas, often incorrectly called 17-year locusts, emerge from the ground in huge numbers over a short period of time, and then disappear for more than a decade. This category is for recipes featuring actual cicadas as an ingredient, and related information about harvesting and preparing them.

443232.description: Sushi actually began as a way of preserving fish. The raw, cleaned fish was pressed between rice and salt by a heavy stone for a few weeks. After a few weeks, the stone was removed and replaced with a light cover. A few months after that, the fermented fish and rice were considered ready to eat. Not until the 18th century did a chef named Yohei decide to serve sushi in its present form and forget about the fermentation process altogether. The use of vinegar rice, however, probably dates back to the fermented taste of early sushi.   In Osaka there is still an elaborate tradition of sushi pressed with rice in wooden boxes. This type of sushi is called hako-zushi. The sushi most commonly known among Westerners comes from Edo, the old name for Tokyo, and consists of hand-rolled sushi specifically called nigiri sushi.     Sashimi is fresh, raw, chilled, sliced, and elegantly arranged. Ideally, sashimi is best when fresh, but most fish freeze well and are served after thawing. Sashimi may be garnished with raw vegetables, leaves of knot grass, parsley, lettuce, shredded daikon, and sometimes seaweed or cucumber. Sashimi is odorless and very delicate. When sliced thick it is served with soy sauce, when sliced thin served with ponzu, a citrus flavored sauce. Wasabi, red pepper, and green onions may be served to mix with sauces as well.    Maki sushi contains strips of fish or vegetables rolled in rice and wrapped in crisp, thin sheets of dried seaweed. There are many combinations that even the most timid can enjoy such as smoked salmon, fresh crab, or shrimp. The adventurous can sample delicacies like octopus, raw clams, sea urchin, or salted fish roe.   Nigiri sushi is a slice of fish (cooked or uncooked) pressed by hand onto a pad of rice. Fish roe is also served as nigiri sushi in a style called gunkan, meaning "boat." Nigiri sushi contains a hint of horseradish and is meant to be dipped in soy sauce. They are always served in pairs.

443254.title: Ukrainian
443254.description: This category lists English-language sites containing recipes and cooking information for Ukrainian cuisine. "Ukrainian cuisine stems from peasant dishes based on grains and staple vegetables like potatoes, cabbage, beets and mushrooms. Meat is typically boiled, fried or stewed. Desserts are usually laden with honey and fruit, mainly cherries and plums, and often baked into sweet breads. While the small dumplings known as varenyky (perogies) are by far the most popular Ukrainian snack, the sacred dish is salo - pig fat. Salo consumption goes back centuries, and Ukrainians age and prize it as obsessively as the French do wine. Borshch originated in Ukraine and is still the national soup; the beet and mixed-vegetable broth is typically served with cream." Source: Lonely Planet's Guide to Ukraine

443314.title: Cajun-Creole
443314.description: This category is for cooking and recipe sites devoted to the cuisine of Louisiana.      Cajun- The cuisine of the descendants of the Acadian French people who migrated to South Louisiana from Nova Scotia.  The cuisine is characterized by the use of pork fat, heavy use of cayenne pepper and hot sauces, and indigenous wildlife and plants.     Creole- The cuisine of the French upper class in South Louisiana, based more on traditional French cooking.  It is characterized by the use of butter instead of pork fat and generally is not as heavily spiced as Cajun cuisine.     Creole cuisine was heavily influenced by the other cultural groups in New Orleans such as the Spanish and other Europeans, Caribbean Islanders,  Africans, African-Americans, and Native Americans.

442540.title: Attachment Parenting
442540.description: Attachment parenting, to put it most simply, is believing what we know in our heart to be true. And if we do that, we find that we trust the child. We trust him in these ways:    We trust that he is doing the very best he can at every given moment, given all of his experiences up to that time.   We trust that though he may be small in size, he is as fully human as we are, and as deserving as we are to have his needs taken seriously.   We trust that he has been born innocent, loving, and trusting. We do not need to "turn him around", to teach him that life is difficult, or train him to be a loving human being - he is that at birth and all we need to do is celebrate that, and support and sustain it.   We don't have to give him lessons about life - life brings its own lessons and its own frustrations.   We recognize that in a very beautiful way, our child teaches us - if we listen - what love is.    We understand that if a child "misbehaves", instead of reacting to the behavior, we should always examine what has been taking place in his life: what stresses, frustrations or frightening, confusing, or difficult situations he has just experienced. We also need to examine whether we have brought about any of these experiences, intentionally or not. It is our job to be responsive parents, meeting the needs of our child; it is not the child's job to meet our needs for a quiet and perfectly well-behaved child.   We understand that It is unfair and unrealistic to expect a child to behave perfectly at all times; after all, no adult can do this either. Yet behind all punishment is the unstated expectation that a child can and should behave perfectly at all times; there is no leeway.   We see that so-called "bad behavior" is in reality nothing more than the child's attempt to communicate an important need in the best way he can, given the present circumstances and all of his prior experience. "Misbehavior" is a signal to us that important needs are not being met. - by us or by others in the child's life. We should not ignore that behavior any more than we should ignore the sound of a smoke detector. We should instead see "bad behavior" as an opportunity - an opportunity to reevaluate our own behavior, to learn about our child's needs, and to meet those needs in the best way possible.   [This definition of attachment parenting is by Jan Hunt, M.Sc., of http://www.naturalchild.org]

444959.title: Bonsai and Suiseki
444959.description: Bonsai (lit. bon-planted) is the art of aesthetic miniaturization of trees, or of developing woody or semi-woody plants shaped as trees, by growing them in containers. Cultivation includes techniques for shaping, watering, and re-potting in various styles of containers.   "Bonsai" is a Japanese pronunciation of the earlier Chinese term penzai. A "bon" is a tray-like pot typically used in bonsai culture. The word bonsai is used in the West as an umbrella term for all miniature trees in containers or pots.     Suiseki, viewing stones, Chinese scholars' stones, and rock penjing are  included in this category.   They all deal with the appreciation of naturally created (as distinct from carved) stones of relatively small size.  If you could call it a boulder, it probably wouldn't qualify as a suiseki.  These stones are appreciated for what they suggest visually, rather than for the monetary value of their mineral content.

444851.title: Gardens
444851.description: This area lists two categories of website: 1. Sites about actual gardens - public gardens, private gardens, botanical gardens, arboreta, personal garden pages. 2. Sites about particular styles of gardens, including examples of such gardens, tips for creating them, etc. Sites that contain information detailing how to achieve certain effects within a garden are listed here, as well as those showcasing their own achievements with a particular style. Sites are categorized according to their main focus. If a public, private, or personal garden site focuses (almost) exclusively on a particular style of garden, you'll find it in the category for that style. Gardens whose style doesn't neatly fall into the style categories are filed in the general public, private, personal, or community garden categories. Sites that sell products or showcase businesses are not listed here.

links.title: I Love Gardens
links.description: Directory of public and private gardens in the US, each with a brief summary and a link to the facility's website.

links.title: The Garden Conservancy
links.description: US organization founded to preserve exceptional American gardens for the public’s education and enjoyment.  Overview of projects and gardens, and calendar of events and programs.

444861.title: Alpine
444861.description: This category lists websites dedicated to alpine and rock gardening. Some document a particular public, private or personal garden designed in this style, while others give information, tips, and tricks related to this garden style.

links.title: Magnars Arctic Alpines and Perennials
links.description: Norwegian gardener North of the Arctic circle presents photos of his garden and plants.

links.title: Franz Hadacek's Alpines and Bulbs

444856.title: Community
444856.description: Websites related to community gardening, where members of the community tend gardens in public or communal spaces.  This includes gardens providing produce for members of the community as well as allotment gardens in which individuals tend small lots within a larger garden area.    This category includes sites for specific gardens, community gardening organizations, and forums/other resources on the topic.

links.title: Denver Urban Gardens
links.description: Nonprofit organization overseeing more than 70 community gardens in the Denver area, dedicated to transforming inner-city lots into lush oases for the community.  Information, education and events, drought guide.

links.title: German Community Gardens

links.title: American Community Gardening Association
links.description: The ACGA is an organization of professionals, volunteers and supporters of community greening in urban and rural communities.

links.title: Long Beach Organic

links.title: Evergreen

links.title: Green Guerillas

links.title: Growing Gardens

links.title: M'Finda Kalunga Garden

links.title: Houzz - Community Gardens

links.title: Eagle Heights Community Garden
links.description: Organic garden associated with the University of Wisconsin (Madison).  Information on plot applications, policies, resources, and programs.

links.title: Garten Rosa Rose

links.title: Northey Street City Farm

links.title: Unity Gardens

links.title: Westbury Community Garden
links.description: Allotments in the city of Houston, Texas. History, information about membership, volunteering and crops, and news archives.

444862.title: Cottage

Some document a particular public, private or personal garden designed in this style, while others give information, tips, and tricks related to this garden style.

links.title: Houzz - The Cottage Garden
links.description: Forum for the discussion cottage gardens, defined as informal, country-style gardens.

links.title: My Enchanting Cottage Garden
links.description: Judy's cottage garden. A blog for passionate gardeners with an emphasis on the quaint English cottage garden style.

444866.title: Japanese
444866.description: This category lists websites dedicated to gardens in the Japanese style. Some document a particular public, private or personal garden designed in this style, while others give information, tips, and tricks related to this garden style.

links.title: Anderson Japanese Gardens
links.description: Acclaimed public garden on 14 acres in Rockford, Illinois. History, photo gallery, and visitor information.

links.title: Marc Peter Keane
links.description: A licensed landscape architect, garden designer, writer, and artist who has lived in Kyoto, Japan for the past 15 years. Portfolio of garden designs.

links.title: Japanese Gardens

links.title: George's Japanese Garden

links.title: Japanese Garden Journal

444868.title: Low Allergen

444867.title: Personal

links.title: Harriet Squier's Flower Garden

links.title: Alison King's Cactus and Succulent Garden

links.title: The Wild Gardener

links.title: Rob's Plants

links.title: Stoy Garden

links.title: Lozinski's Gardens

links.title: Turning Toward the Light

links.title: Hannelotte's Garden

links.title: The Gardening Guru's How-To Website

links.title: Janet's Garden
links.description: Weblog for a small USDA zone 4 garden seeks to inform with cultural tips and personal experiences with plants.

links.title: Garden Djinn
links.description: The journal of a gardener in transition from her former garden (Hogglebog, a zone 5 garden located in southeast Michigan) to her new, as yet unnamed garden in Phoenix, Arizona

links.title: Stern's Splendors of the Rainforest
links.description: Michigan gardener specializes in growing orchids, cacti, and bromeliads indoors and in a greenhouse. Photo albums, Michigan gardening links.

links.title: Sue Haywards Garden Design
links.description: UK. Gardening layout and design, gardening Latin and trivia, favorite plants and photos of her English garden online. The site owner has earned a National Certificate in Horticulture.

links.title: Ilona's Garden
links.description: Ohio gardener presents a collection of garden writings, plant highlights, and garden task calendar for the midwest.

links.title: My Little Vegetable Garden
links.description: Updates and information on a fruit and vegetable garden in Malaysia. Full of photos and whimsical observations.

links.title: Larvalbug's Garden
links.description: Features well written, photo-illustrated short articles about the plants and wildlife in an Austin, Texas garden, and a detailed garden overview with map.

links.title: Peggy's Garden Gallery
links.description: Excellent photo gallery and information on gardening.

links.title: Harriet's Home And Garden
links.description: Family site showcasing a shady Kentucky garden and its pond.

links.title: Growing The Home Garden
links.description: Home gardener in Tennessee shares information, garden photos, projects, and stories.

links.title: The Real Scottish Vegetable Garden
links.description: Writing about experiences as an amateur grow-your-own gardener in Scotland.

444864.title: Private
444864.description: Descriptions, photos, and information about private gardens of renown around the world.  Gardens featured in the websites listed here are not routinely open to the public, but may be open by appointment or invitation.  Examples include gardens designed by famous garden architects, or gardens known from television shows and gardening magazines.  Websites listed here are descriptive, focusing more on the garden than the gardener or the process of gardening.  They often include sections on the garden's history and development, its design philosophy, and photo galleries.

links.title: Tasmanian Gardeners Create Eden
links.description: An account of how a Tasmanian couple built their own Eden, in narrative and photos.

links.title: Maggie's Garden in Texas
links.description: Multi-faceted gardening site centered on a family garden.  Plant portraits, visual tours, forums, tips and guides.

links.title: Dublin Garden Group
links.description: Private gardens that are open to the public in Dublin,  Ireland.

links.title: Davi's Garden Tour
links.description: Stroll through traditional home garden on the Mornington Peninsula in Victoria, Australia, past plenty of flowers, native plants, pets, and bird visitors.

links.title: Back Yard
links.description: Photos and descriptions of plants in a backyard garden in Maryland, and a peek at its construction project.

links.title: Offene Gartenpforte
links.description: Hobby gardeners of Niederrhein (Germany) gardening association show their private gardens in photographs.  Dates for current-year garden tours.

links.title: Olympic Views

links.title: Moosey's Country Garden

links.title: OpDeHaar Gardens
links.description: Garden in a wooded area of the Netherlands featuring many woodland and shade plants, as well as numerous varieties of acers, magnolia, rhododendron, camellia, bamboo, ferns and hosta. Visits by appointment.

links.title: Darts Hill Garden Park

links.title: Lady Anne's Garden of Eden

links.title: Jim Handtmann's LandEscapes
links.description: Small, meticulously tended backyard garden in Minneapolis.    Tours by way of thumbnail galleries.

links.title: My Ulster Garden
links.description: A monthly record in pictures of the main features of this Northern Ireland garden.

links.title: A Southern Garden
links.description: Describes creation of stately garden in Florence, Alabama, along with many of its plants. Nicely illustrated.

444869.title: Public
444869.description: Descriptions, photos, and information about gardens around the world that are routinely open to the public.

links.title: Montreal Estate Gardens

links.title: International Peace Garden

links.title: National Botanic Garden of Belgium
links.description: Botanical garden near Brussels. Overview of history, mission, and educational opportunities, visitor information, and calendar of events.

links.title: St. George Village Botanical Garden

links.title: Bermuda's Gardens
links.description: Illustrated listing with information on garden destinations in Bermuda.

links.title: The Botanical Garden of the University of Vienna
links.description: Specialized in mountain flora, pharmaceutical plants, and succulents, with special collections and a tropical greenhouse. Overview, and information about visiting.

links.title: Gardenvisit.com
links.description: A guide to garden tours and history, historic parks, and botanic collections open to the public in the UK, USA, Europe, Japan, India, and Australia.

links.title: University of Copenhagen: Botanical Garden & Museum

links.title: Peter Korns Trädgården

links.title: University of Zagreb Botanical Garden
links.description: Overview of the gardens areas and collections, with history and tour information.

links.title: University of Helsinki Botanical Garden at Kaisaniemi
links.description: Maintaining a collection of living plants for use in research and teaching. Information about public and research collections, greenhouses, and tours.

links.title: The Rockhampton Botanic Gardens

links.title: Cowra Japanese Garden
links.description: Pleasure garden in New South Wales, with a strolling garden, water features, stone garden, and teahouse. Information about visiting, events, and group travel.

444870.title: Canada
444870.description: Gardens open to the public in Canada

links.title: The Butchart Gardens
links.description: Offers fifty acres of floral finery with best times to visit.  Provides a full history of the gardens. Located in Victoria, BC.

links.title: Minter Country Garden

links.title: Muttart Conservatory

links.title: Royal Botanical Gardens

links.title: The Arboretum at the University of Guelph

links.title: University of British Columbia Botanical Garden and Centre for Plant Research

links.title: Harriet Irving Botanical Gardens

links.title: VanDusen Botanical Garden

links.title: Coastal Maine Botanical Gardens
links.description: Gardens and natural areas in Boothbay include fern, wetlands, and native plant shoreland gardens, a collection of rhododendrons, and a trail lined with mosses, lichens, heaths and ferns. Information about the garden, events, and membership.

links.title: Merryspring
links.description: Nature center and park in Camden, with nature trails and gardens open to the public free of charge. Overview of programs and gardens, with calendar and information on wildlife and native plants.

links.title: Adkins Arboretum
links.description: Native garden and preserve on Maryland’s Eastern shore dedicated to promoting the appreciation and conservation of the region’s native plants. Information about programs and events, research, and the native plant nursery.

links.title: Ladew Topiary Gardens
links.description: Topiary and flower gardens plus a nature walk and historic home. Includes events calendar, history and rental information.

links.title: Cylburn Arboretum Association
links.description: Nature preserve and city park in Baltimore. Information about visiting, history, and educational programs.

links.title: Brookside Gardens
links.description: Public display garden in Wheaton, featuring floral displays, plant collections, conservatories, and a horticultural library.

links.title: Historic London Town & Gardens
links.description: County park located on the South River in Edgewater, with in its boundaries part of the historic town of London, which is being excavated by archaeologists. The naturalized woodland shade garden includes plantings of bloodroot, trillium, lady’s slipper, hardy orchids and other natives.

links.title: Arnold Arboretum
links.description: Research and educational institution in Boston.  It manages a collection of hardy trees, shrubs, and vines located on 265 acres and associated herbarium and library collections.

links.title: Berkshire Botanical Garden
links.description: This garden's collections emphasize plants that thrive in the Berkshires, and are displayed in an informal, country setting. Also offers community events, and classes for all ages and skill levels.

links.title: The Polly Hill Arboretum
links.description: A non-profit horticultural and botanical center on Martha's Vineyard.  Provides information on admission, membership, events and programs.

links.title: New England Botanic Garden at Tower Hill
links.description: Operated by Worcester County Horticultural Society, this garden features several distinctive theme areas. Information about visiting, workshops and events, history, and membership.

links.title: The Botanic Garden at Smith College
links.description: A collection of thousands of plants on the college campus in Northampton, grown in the Lyman Conservatory and outdoors in various gardens, and scattered throughout the campus arboretum. Photo gallery, academic and cultural events, history, and information about the herbarium.

links.title: Mount Holyoke College Botanic Garden
links.description: Greenhouse, gardens, and arboretum in South Hadley, featuring several specialty gardens and collections. Information about education, research, and annual flower show.

links.title: Anna Scripps Whitcomb Conservatory
links.description: The oldest continually-running conservatory in the USA. History, visitor information, and photographs. Located in Detroit, Michigan.

links.title: Fernwood Botanical Gardens & Nature Preserve
links.description: A living museum located in the orchard country of southwest Michigan with valuable collections and delicate ecosystems. Includes a Japanese garden, a ravine garden, fern trail, and an arboretum.

links.title: Frederik Meijer Gardens & Sculpture Park
links.description: Collection of scenic gardens in Grand Rapids augmented by sculpture located throughout. Includes a butterfly garden, nature trail, conservatory, and shade garden. Information about visiting, gardens, plants, and artwork, exhibits, and events.

links.title: Leila Arboretum
links.description: Part of the park system of Battle Creek, the arboretum includes a collection of mature specimen trees, many dating back to the 1920’s, and also features a children's garden. Information about events and classes, volunteering, and membership.

links.title: Hidden Lake Gardens
links.description: Garden in Tipton features thousands of labeled trees, shrubs, and flowers, with collections of tropical and arid plants, flowering houseplants, dwarf and rare conifers. Also offers five miles of marked hiking trails.  Map of the gardens, and information about classes and programs.

links.title: Dow Gardens
links.description: Horticultural and educational garden in Midland showcases its collections, displays, children's and woodland gardens, and history.

links.title: Matthaei Botanical Gardens
links.description: This University of Michigan facility includes a conservatory with exotic plants from around the world, nature trails, mature woodlands, wetlands, several ponds, and a tall grass prairie.

links.title: Slayton Arboretum at Hillsdale College
links.description: Displays and preserves living plant collections and native plant communities, and conducts research, education, and public outreach programs. Information about activities, events, and children's garden.

links.title: Munsinger Clemens Botanical Society
links.description: The Munsinger Garden and Clemens Garden are located on the banks of the Mississippi in St. Cloud (Minnesota). They offer informal flower gardens, wooded areas, and various specialty gardens. Information about gardens, events, and membership.

links.title: Minnesota Landscape Arboretum
links.description: Large public garden area featuring annual and perennial display gardens, collections of plants for Northern climates, natural and native areas, and demonstration gardens. Information about visiting, tours, and research.

links.title: The Carleton College Cowling Arboretum
links.description: Large facility adjacent to the Northfield campus, serving education, conservation, and recreation purposes with its woodland and prairie habitats. Overview of flora and fauna, and visitor information.

444900.title: Mississippi
444900.description: Gardens open to the public, located in Mississippi.

links.title: Mynelle Gardens
links.description: Botanical garden in Jackson, with 7 acres of plantings including water features and sculpture. Photos and basic visitor information.

links.title: Crosby Arboretum
links.description: A facility of Mississippi State University at Picayune dedicated to showcasing and preserving native plants of the U.S. south.

links.title: Missouri Botanical Garden
links.description: Garden in St. Louis renowned for its fundamental botanical research, horticultural displays and education programs. Includes a butterfly house and nature preserve.

links.title: Mizzou Botanic Garden
links.description: Living museum in Columbia displaying thousands of plants amongst famous icons, such as Jefferson's original grave marker. Descriptions of the many specialty gardens, visitor information, newsletter, and FAQ.

444916.title: Montana
444916.description: Gardens open to the public, located in Montana.

links.title: Tizer Gardens
links.description: High-altitude garden featuring rose, patriotic, and herb gardens, an old-time vegetable garden, wildlife gardens, and a Lewis and Clark native plant trail.

444895.title: Nebraska
444895.description: Gardens open to the public, located in Nebraska.

links.title: Nebraska Statewide Arboretum
links.description: Includes a collection of trees and other plants that are used for education, research and enjoyment. Helps communities and people create forested and garden environments. Lists services, staff, and related links.

links.title: Lauritzen Gardens - Omaha's Botanical Center
links.description: The gardens contain over 100 acres of flower and plant displays from around the world. View events, educational opportunities, clubs, visitor information, and exhibits.

444905.title: Nevada
444905.description: Gardens open to the public, located in Nevada.

links.title: Springs Preserve
links.description: Cultural institution in Las Vegas featuring botanical gardens and an interpretive trail system through a scenic wetland habitat, along with museums, galleries, and outdoor events.

links.title: The Fells
links.description: Located in Newbury by Lake Sunapee, this former private summer retreat blends formal and naturalistic gardens, including a large rock garden.  Overview, photos, visitor information, and calendar of events.

links.title: Friends of the Frelinghuysen Arboretum
links.description: Volunteer organization dedicated to various horticultural facilities in Morris County (New Jersey), especially its headquarters location, the George Griswold Frelinghuysen Arboretum. Information about the Frelinghuysen Arboretum, history, events, and workshops.

links.title: Van Vleck House & Gardens
links.description: On this suburban estate in Montclair, formal gardens featuring a choice collection of rhododendrons, azaleas, and other broad-leaved evergreens extend from a turn-of-the-century Italianate villa. History, visitor information, calendar of events.

links.title: Somerset County Parks
links.description: Gardens tended by the park commission include the naturalistic Leonard J. Buck Garden, fragrance, rose, and perennial gardens, and an arboretum.

links.title: Greenwood Gardens
links.description: Historic estate garden in Short Hills (New Jersey), being restored for public enjoyment as a project of the Garden Conservancy.  History, photos, mission statement.

links.title: Reeves-Reed Arboretum
links.description: Suburban conservancy on a historic country estate in Summit, dedicated to the environment and horticultural education. News, and information about visiting and events.

links.title: Duke Farms
links.description: Large estate garden in Hillsborough, whose features include a lake and other water features, a sycamore allee, and barns. Information about recreation and education, and nature programs.

links.title: Rutgers Gardens
links.description: Campus arboretum and public garden. Information about collections and theme gardens, visiting, educational programs, and events.

links.title: David C. Shaw Arboretum
links.description: County park facility in Freehold, featuring hundreds of species, cultivars, and varieties of ornamental trees and shrubs. Summary and visiting information.

links.title: Morven Museum & Garden
links.description: House built before the American Revolution by Richard Stockton. The former governor's mansion is now a state museum. Information about museum exhibits and garden tours.

444883.title: New Mexico
444883.description: Gardens open to the public, located in New Mexico.

links.title: Santa Fe Botanical Garden
links.description: Encompasses the Ortiz Mountains Education Preserve and the Leonora Curtin Wetland Preserve. Information about nature, geology, and history, as well as volunteering, membership, and events.

444882.title: New York
444882.description: Public gardens in New York state

links.title: Sonnenberg Gardens
links.description: Now a New York State Historic Park, the gardens accompanying the Victorian mansion, located in Canandaigua, comprise several distinct designs. Guided tours, visitor information, schedule of events.

links.title: Wave Hill
links.description: Famous public garden in the northwest Bronx along the Hudson River, with flower gardens, alpine house, greenhouses, and cultural center. Visitor information, events, membership, volunteering opportunities.

links.title: Old Westbury Gardens
links.description: Built in 1906, this garden in Old Westbury is an example of period landscape design, with formal gardens and landscaped grounds.  Visitor information and photo tour for mansion and gardens.

links.title: Buffalo and Erie County Botanical Gardens
links.description: Features a glass conservatory designed by Frederick Law Olmsted with tropical and desert gardens, an arboretum and pinetum, shrub garden, and bog garden. History, education programs, events, virtual tour.

links.title: The New York Botanical Garden
links.description: Garden in the Bronx consists of 28 specialty gardens, including a conservatory, a children's adventure garden, and a 40-acre old-growth forest. Information about entertainment and educational activities.

links.title: Planting Fields Arboretum State Historic Park
links.description: Long Island public arboretum and historic site with greenhouses, gardens, woodland paths, and outstanding plant collections. The grounds were landscaped by the Olmsted brothers. History and mission, event calendar, cultural activities.

links.title: Ross Park Zoo and Gardens
links.description: Zoo in Binghamton also includes botanical gardens, including a hosta garden, a butterfly garden, an ornamental grass garden, an iris garden and a memorial garden.  Virtual tour, calendar of events, and quarterly newsletter archive.

links.title: Brooklyn Botanic Garden
links.description: Offers news, virtual tour, programs, events, articles, shopping, research, and information for visitors.

links.title: Linwood Gardens
links.description: This private garden located near Rochester, New York, features a significant collection of American tree peonies. It is open to the public on a number of days in June and July.

links.title: Clark Botanic Garden
links.description: Educational facility in Long Island featuring native spring wildflowers, conifers, roses, perennials, wetland and rock garden plants, medicinal plants and collections of particular plant families.

links.title: Queens Botanical Garden
links.description: Created as an exhibit at the 1939 New York World's Fair, the garden features with rose, bee, herb, and perennial gardens, changing displays, and public programs. Educational programs and plant listings.

links.title: Bayard Cutting Arboretum
links.description: State park on Long Island noted both for its plant collection and its variety of bird species. Information on flora and fauna, programs, and publications.

links.title: Gardens at Cricket Hill Farm
links.description: Garden in the Hudson Valley designed for low maintenance, four-season interest, and bird life, offering tours, workshops, and plant sales.

links.title: Cornell Botanic Gardens
links.description: Holds, manages, protects, and enhances the living botanical collections and the natural areas and gorges of Cornell for the benefit of the community. Information about collections, visiting, education, and publications.

links.title: JC Raulston Arboretum
links.description: Features a diverse collection of plants adapted for landscape use in the southeastern United States, with a focus on hardy shrubs and trees. Full-featured website with details and photos for many of the plant holdings. Piedmont.

links.title: Airlie Gardens
links.description: Quintessential Southern garden in Wilmington featuring azaleas, camellias, statuary and the historic Airlie Oak, and large freshwater lakes. Virtual tour, information about events, education, membership, and volunteering.

links.title: Daniel Stowe Botanical Garden
links.description: Garden in Belmont, offers community and camp programs, classes, and group tours. Calendar of events, membership details, searchable plant information, volunteer opportunities.

links.title: The Sarah P. Duke Gardens
links.description: The crown jewel of Duke University, renowned both for landscape design and the quality of horticulture. Information about visiting, events, and gardening, and a section just for kids.

links.title: Wing Haven
links.description: A four-acre garden in a residential neighborhood of Charlotte, with formal gardens, water features, and wooded areas. Garden tour, membership, volunteer, and calendar information.

links.title: Morrison Gardens
links.description: A rose garden in Davidson featuring 110 cultivars of heritage, antique and old Roses. Site features photos,  gardening tips and heritage rose information.

links.title: Cape Fear Botanical Garden
links.description: Teaching and pleasure garden featuring wooded areas with nature trails, waterwise, heritage, and children's gardens, and collections of camellias and daylilies. Descriptions and photos, events calendar, and plant list by month of bloom.

links.title: UNC Charlotte Botanical Gardens
links.description: Combination of outdoor and indoor garden facilities on campus, including a woodland garden featuring a large rhododendron collection, an Oriental-themed ornamental garden, and a tropical greenhouse.

links.title: The Elizabethan Gardens
links.description: Garden in the formal British style on Roanoke Island in the Outer Banks. Photographs of garden areas, admission information.

links.title: Wilson Rose Garden
links.description: Tour, history, and general information about this garden in Eastern North Carolina.

links.title: Franklin Park Conservatory
links.description: Glasshouse in Columbus featuring several collections of plants from different habitats.  Virtual tour, educational programs, visitor information.

links.title: The Dawes Arboretum
links.description: Facility near Columbus with large collections of woody plants, as well as natural areas.  Photos, history, events, reports, collections, and visitor information.

links.title: Mill Creek MetroParks
links.description: Part of this recreation and preservation area in Mahoning Valley are Fellows Riverside Gardens, with large spring bulb displays, and collections of woody plants, perennials, and roses. Visitor information and photos.

links.title: Kingwood Center
links.description: A 47-acre former estate garden in Mansfield, with collections of peonies, herbs and roses, daylilies and irises, as well as general display gardens. Open free to the public. Includes visitor and membership information.

links.title: Chadwick Arboretum at Ohio State University
links.description: Located on the Columbus agriculture campus. Information about staff and programs, plant sale, and directions.

links.title: The Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Garden
links.description: The botanical gardens interspersed with the zoo areas include pollinator, butterfly, and oriental gardens, a dinosaur garden, wetland trails, and an endangered species area.

links.title: Cox Arboretum & Gardens Metropark
links.description: 189 acres of gardens and natural areas in Dayton. Provides descriptions of specialty gardens, information about the history, schedule of events, visiting and volunteering information.

444904.title: Oklahoma
444904.description: Gardens open to the public, located in Oklahoma.

links.title: Hoyt Arboretum
links.description: Non-profit greenspace located two miles from downtown Portland. Among the tree collections, the magnolias and conifers are especially renowned. Offers nature-focused instruction, and information about events and volunteering.

links.title: The Oregon Garden
links.description: Attraction in historic Silverton, featuring water features, garden art, wetlands, a rediscovery forest, a kids' garden, and a house designed by Frank Lloyd Wright. Photos, news, information about events and classes.

links.title: Japanese Garden
links.description: Authentic Japanese garden in Portland's West hills, whose areas include a strolling pond garden, a tea garden, and a sand and stone garden. Description and photos, and information about visiting and events.

links.title: Lan Su Chinese Garden
links.description: The official site for the Garden of Awakening Orchids, a traditional Chinese garden built in the heart of Portland.

links.title: Portland Parks and Recreation
links.description: Includes rose and rhododendron gardens, a memory garden, Leach Botanical Garden, and community gardens. Photos, descriptions, visiting information, and event schedules.

links.title: Mount Pisgah Arboretum
links.description: Recreation and nature park in Eugene. Includes trail maps, festival and event listings, history and outdoor education programs.

links.title: Rogerson Clematis Collection
links.description: Collection housed in a garden and greenhouse, embracing both species and cultivars. General information, history and mission.

links.title: Chanticleer Garden
links.description: Descriptions, photos, history, and admission information for eclectically designed estate garden near Philadelphia.

links.title: Longwood Gardens
links.description: Horticultural display garden near Philadelphia created by Pierre duPont in 19th century.  Visitor information, schedule of events, what's in bloom,  history, education, and employment opportunities.

links.title: Tyler Arboretum
links.description: Its 650-acre grounds near Philadelphia include a pinetum, a native woodland walk, and various flowering shrub and tree collections.

links.title: Lake Erie Arboretum at Frontier Park
links.description: Several hundred tree species planted in a riparian zone of the Erie park, serving as an educational facility. Tree fact sheets provided by student projects.

links.title: The Gardens at Morris Arboretum
links.description: The official arboretum of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, whose thousands of woody plants include many of Philadelphia's oldest, rarest, and largest trees, is set in a Victorian landscape garden of winding paths, streams, flowers and special garden areas.

links.title: Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
links.description: Pittsburgh institution with indoor and outdoor collections. History, photo tour of the gardens, database of species, and information about research, educational classes, and special exhibits and events.

links.title: The Scott Arboretum of Swarthmore College
links.description: Encompassing more than 300 acres of the college campus and exhibiting thousands of ornamental plant species, the arboretum displays trees, shrubs, vines and perennials. Overview of specialty gardens, and information about visiting and events.

links.title: Bartram's Garden
links.description: America's oldest living botanical garden features an 18th century farmstead, native plants, wildflower meadow, and wetland. Located in Philadelphia.

links.title: Churchville Nature Center
links.description: This Bucks county facility includes a visitor center with interpretive exhibits, and indoor and outdoor wildlife viewing areas. Developed for education, preservation, and conservation. Information on the facilities and events.

links.title: Jenkins Arboretum
links.description: Horticultural showcase of native trees, shrubs, rhododendrons, azaleas, laurel, blueberries, ferns and wildflowers in Devon. Information about membership and events, map, and photo galleries.

links.title: Awbury Arboretum
links.description: Historic home and gardens in Philadelphia. Information on upcoming events, volunteering, summer nature program, and history.

links.title: Haverford College Arboretum
links.description: Features nature trails, a duck pond, a pinetum, a Japanese Zen garden and an herb garden. Includes virtual tour with numerous photos, history, calendar of events and membership information.

links.title: Bowman's Hill Wildflower Preserve
links.description: 134 acres in New Hope featuring hundreds of species of native plants, in a setting of picturesque woodlands, meadows, a pond and a creek. Information about gardening with native plants, visiting, educational programs, and events.

links.title: Graver Arboretum
links.description: Park associated with Muhlenberg college, located in the northern Lehigh Valley, featuring a wide variety of trees (especially conifers) and wildflowers in a natural setting.

links.title: Hershey Gardens
links.description: Pleasure garden established by Milton Hershey, featuring many themed gardens, seasonal displays, unique trees, an outdoor butterfly house, and a large rose collection. Information about visiting, educational programs, and events.

links.title: Silver Lake Nature Center
links.description: A 253 acre park in Bristol featuring various habitats characteristic of the Atlantic coastal plain. Programs and events schedule, trail map and contact details.

links.title: Henry Schmieder Arboretum
links.description: Associated with the Department of Ornamental Horticulture and Environmental Design of Delaware Valley University. Information for visitors and volunteers, and seasonal programs. Doylestown.

links.title: Mill Fleurs
links.description: Large private garden in Point Pleasant (Bucks County), open for guided and open tours. Peak season for the mostly shaded property is spring. Also an on-site rare plant nursery.

links.title: Riverbanks Zoo and Garden
links.description: The lushly planted botanical gardens accompanying this zoo in Columbia are arranged into several climatic and theme gardens. Descriptions, photos, and visitor information.

links.title: Brookgreen Gardens
links.description: Hours and information on this park with the first sculpture garden in the US; listed on the National Register of Historic Places and located in Pawleys Island.

links.title: Kalmia Gardens
links.description: Landscaped gardens at Coker College in Hartsville. Presents history, a photographic tour and collage, and staff information.

444889.title: South Dakota
444889.description: Gardens open to the public, located in South Dakota.

links.title: McCrory Gardens
links.description: South Dakota State University facility in Brookings, includes prairie and rock gardens, a children's maze, and tree collections. History and garden overview.

links.title: Cheekwood Botanical Garden and Museum of Art
links.description: This garden in Nashville includes a Japanese garden, herb, perennial and wildflower gardens, as well as a woodland sculpture trail and a nature sanctuary. Photo tours, overview of gardens, and visitor information.

links.title: Memphis Botanic Garden
links.description: Encompasses lakes, woodlands, and display gardens, including a rose garden, a Japanese garden, a sensory garden, Photos, calendar of events, volunteer news, and membership information.

links.title: The Dixon Gallery and Gardens
links.description: The gardens surrounding the art museum, laid out amidst mature woodland, include formal and cutting gardens, woodland gardens, and sculpture. History and descriptions.

links.title: The Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden
links.description: Features landscaped acres of trees, gardens, and lawns, with fountains, sculptures, and historic mansions. Membership information, photos of each garden, and information about educational programs.

links.title: Fort Worth Botanic Garden
links.description: The oldest botanic garden in Texas, a 109-acre living museum displaying over 2,500 species of native and exotic plants.

links.title: Riverside Nature Center
links.description: Located in Kerrville on the Guadaqlupe River, this former farm has been transformed into an urban wildlife and native plant sanctuary, with an arboretum, cacti, wildflowers, and native grasses. Schedule, visitor and membership information.

links.title: San Antonio Botanical Garden
links.description: City garden features formal and display gardens, a conservatory, and sections representing Texas native areas. Offers educational events, programs, and classes year-round.

links.title: Amarillo Botanical Gardens
links.description: Site documents the ongoing construction of a new garden and conservatory facility. Information about volunteering, events, and associated garden clubs.

links.title: South Texas Botanical Gardens & Nature Center
links.description: The cultivated gardens feature a large collections of orchids, hibiscus, plumeria, and roses, as well as a sensory garden, offset by the surrounding wetlands and mesquite forest. Information about history, visiting, kids' activities, and event calendar.

links.title: Chandor Gardens
links.description: Estate in Weatherford containing a 40-foot manmade waterfall, Chinese rock sculptures, and an English lawn bowling green. Picture gallery, garden history, and visitor information.

links.title: John Fairey Garden
links.description: Garden in Hempstead featuring a collection of rare plants native to the Southern US and Mexico, mingled with Asian plants, with a dry garden, arboretum, and herbaceous border. Beautiful photography, botanical details, visitor information.

links.title: Red Butte Garden
links.description: A non-profit botanical and ecological center provided by University of Utah. Events and activity announcements, e-mail reminders, and user polls.

links.title: USU Botanical Center
links.description: This facility operated by the Utah State University in Kaysville focuses on education, recreation, research, and demonstration projects. It features butterfly, children's, and other themed gardens, ponds, and bird-watching opportunities.

444922.title: Vermont
444922.description: Gardens open to the public, located in Vermont.

links.title: University of Vermont Horticulture Research Center
links.description: Used for agricultural research and education, this facility is home to many trees, shrubs, perennials, apples and small fruit. It is open to visitors, and offers a self-guided tour. Listing of collections, events, and programs.

links.title: George Washington's Mount Vernon Estate and Gardens
links.description: The house and garden where George Washington lived, now an educational tourist attraction.  Formal and plantation gardens.  Visitor information and educational pages.

links.title: The Edith Johnson Carrier Arboretum
links.description: Arboretum on the James Madison University campus also includes herb, bog, rock, and perennial gardens, serving as an outdoor educational and environmental center. Descriptions and photos of the gardens, information about visiting and events.

links.title: Lewis Ginter Botanical Garden
links.description: Richmond attraction features perennial and Victorian gardens, exotic Asian valley, wetland and children's areas, and a study garden. Information about visiting, events, and education.

links.title: Norfolk Botanical Garden
links.description: Features many theme gardens, collections, and an arboretum. Photos and descriptions, visitor information, gardening resources.

links.title: Oatlands Plantation
links.description: Mansion and gardens of an 1803 plantation in Leesburg, a National Trust for Historic Preservation property. The formal gardens are maintained in the spirit of the original owners. Calendar of events, history, rates and directions.

links.title: The Old City Cemetery
links.description: Historic arboretum of 19th-century plantings at a Lynchburg public cemetery. History, and a horticulture and wildlife guide.

links.title: Blandy Experimental Farm
links.description: Research facility in the Shenandoah Valley, home of the State Arboretum of Virginia. Information about education programs for all ages, photo gallery, and FAQ.

links.title: Green Spring Gardens Park
links.description: Public park in Alexandria features a variety of garden styles, including a rock garden, shade garden, herb garden, and backyard wildlife habitat.  Visitor information, downloadable plant information sheets.

444908.title: Washington
444908.description: Public gardens located in Washington state.

links.title: Rhododendron Species Foundation and Botanical Garden
links.description: Garden near Seattle, home to one of the largest rhododendron collections in the world. Information about species, photos gallery, and list of plants and seeds for sale.

links.title: Washington Park Arboretum
links.description: Urban green space on the shores of Lake Washington in Seattle includes collections of Acers and New Zealand natives, and a functional winter garden landscape. Information about visiting and collections, news and events, and seasonal highlights.

links.title: Dunn Gardens
links.description: Garden in suburban Seattle designed by the Olmsted brothers, offering woodland plantings and panoramic views. History, and illustrated pages for many featured plants and trees. Open for guided tours only.

links.title: Kruckeberg Botanic Garden
links.description: Formerly private gardens and collections in Shoreline now open to the public. History, information about visiting and the botanical collections, and volunteer opportunities.

links.title: Glen Echo Garden
links.description: Multiply themed garden in Bellingham, including a begonia and fuchsia garden and a gigantic stump garden. Visitor information and photo gallery.

links.title: Lakewold Gardens
links.description: Estate whose garden areas include rose and knot gardens, alpine scree and rock garden, waterfall, and fern and woodland gardens.

links.title: Whitney Gardens & Nursery
links.description: Seven acres of gardens at the foot of the Olympic mountains known for rare hybrid and species rhododendrons, azaleas, magnolias, trees and shrubs.

links.title: Dumbarton Oaks
links.description: Gardens at the Washington (D.C.) academic library, designed by Beatrix Farrand, which complement its research resources in the history of landscape architecture.  Garden tour in photos.

links.title: United States National Arboretum
links.description: Includes an array of display gardens, collections, and historical monuments set among native stands of eastern deciduous trees. Photo galleries, information about events and research, and horticultural information.

links.title: The United States Botanic Garden
links.description: Located on the Capitol Grounds, this garden features a variety of living exhibits, including seasonal exhibits in the conservatory and Bartholdi Park, and environmental and educational features in the National Garden.

444925.title: West Virginia
444925.description: Gardens open to the public, located in West Virginia.

links.title: The West Virginia University Core Arboretum
links.description: Set in mostly old-growth forest on steep hillside and Monongahela River flood plain, the arboretum offers trails and specimen trees, and is known for its spring ephemeral display. History and virtual tour.

links.title: Green Bay Botanical Garden
links.description: Features display gardens and natural areas, including perennial, cottage, and rose gardens, a children's garden, and a woodland garden. Information about gardening classes, educational programs for schools and special events.

links.title: Olbrich Botanical Gardens
links.description: Includes gardens located on the shores of Lake Monona. Includes outside gardens and an indoor tropical conservatory.

links.title: Rotary Gardens
links.description: An internationally themed botanical garden in Janesville. Summary of collections, photo gallery, information about events and education opportunities.

444877.title: Wyoming
444877.description: Gardens open to the public, located in Wyoming.

links.title: Cheyenne Botanic Gardens
links.description: Traditional public botanic garden, municipal nursery and community garden. The numerous gardens include displays of native, tropical, rose, herb, cacti, inside a conservatory and on the outside grounds.

444865.title: Rain
444865.description:
Rain gardens are landscaped areas, usually planted with native plants, that make use of rainwater runoff in the yard.

For the gardener, rain gardens reclaim rainwater and result in more rainwater soaking into the ground. This also reduces the amount of stormwater runoff carrying pollution and debris into nearby lakes and waterways and helps reduce local flooding.

links.title: Maplewood: Rain Gardens
links.description: Includes garden types, plant lists for Minnesota, design and care guides, and local maps.

links.title: Dave Stack: Rain Gardens
links.description: Introductory guide, concerns, Minnesota native plant list, and links.

links.title: Clean Water Atlanta: Rain Gardens for Home Landscapes
links.description: Instructions on creating a garden and a native plant list for Georgia gardeners.

links.title: Rain Garden Network

1028724.title: Hypertufa
1028724.description: Hypertufa is a man-made rock made from various materials bonded together using Portland cement. It is a porous material, which makes it favorable for plant growth, and also renders items made from hypertufa light compared to ones made from concrete or terracotta.  Hypertufa containers are popular among alpine gardeners, who have found that troughs made from the materials were a suitable (and less expensive) alternative to troughs hewn from natural stone.  Hypertufa is quite variable in its composition, and can be used in various ways, to make containers, rocks, or ornaments. This category presents online resources documenting various recipes for preparing hypertufa, and techniques for its use.

444450.title: Xeriscaping
444450.description: The concept of xeriscape was developed in Denver, Colorado, in response to water shortages. "Xeros" is a Greek word that means "dry." Xeriscape refers to a landscape that uses little supplemental water. It does not refer to a dry, barren landscape, nor is a xeriscape a "no maintenance" landscape. Like traditional landscapes, a xeriscape may be designed to minimize labor or to require frequent care. Many people appreciate beautiful landscapes, but have limited time to spend tending a garden. By using plants that are well adapted, mulches that suppress weeds and conserve water, and drip irrigation to make the most use of water, these landscapes can have color and fragrance with only monthly or seasonal gardening chores. Gardeners who like to spend time in the garden can design a xeriscape to be as labor intensive as a highly maintained traditional garden, but use much less water.

444756.title: Canada
444756.description: The term "Master Gardener" was first coined in the early 1970s to describe a new Agricultural Extension program initiated in the U.S. in Washington State. Since then the idea for organized groups of volunteer gardeners providing information to other interested gardeners has spread into communities all over the United States and Canada.   If you are interested in gardening, we hope you can find a link to Master Gardeners in your location. They are frequently experts in many areas of gardening, and are eager to share valuable information and resources with other interested gardeners.   If you're a member of a state or local Master Gardener chapter, we'd like to know about your web site so we can include it here. It's a great opportunity for master gardeners all over the country to compare notes, share contact information, and exchange ideas and resources.    Enjoy exploring these links and send us your submissions!

444757.title: United States
444757.description: The term "Master Gardener" was first coined in the early 1970s to describe a new Agricultural Extension program initiated in Washington State. Since then the idea for organized groups of volunteer gardeners providing information to other interested gardeners has spread into communities all over the United States and Canada.   If you are interested in gardening, we hope you can find a link to Master Gardeners in your location. They are frequently experts in many areas of gardening, and are eager to share valuable information and resources with other interested gardeners.   If you're a member of a state or local Master Gardener chapter, we'd like to know about your web site so we can include it here. It's a great opportunity for master gardeners all over the country to compare notes, share contact information, and exchange ideas and resources.    Enjoy exploring these links and send us your submissions!

444480.title: Cacti and Succulents
444480.description: Plants that have adjusted to the arid and semi-arid regions   of the world are known as cacti and succulents.  Cacti are    defined as members of one plant family and are considered     separately, although they are actually succulents.  The term  Succulent encompasses all other fleshy plants, which stem     from a variety of plant families.                              Both succulents and cacti have developed means of survival    that assure their growth in these regions.  Their leaves      have become smaller and their stems larger in order to store  more water; in some, the leaves have disappeared leaving      only thickened green stems.  In plants where the leaves       have not disappeared, the leaves may have become thickened    or insulated with coverings of hair, wax or scales.

445027.title: Credit Repair Services
445027.description: Credit repair organizations are generally businesses that, for a fee, will advise consumers on methods they may employ that, if successful, could remove derogatory information from their credit bureau reports, thus making it easier to obtain additional credit.   The Fair Credit Reporting Act was enacted to protect consumers from abusive credit reporting practices and to establish a fair and reasonable framework within which commerce could safely continue to be conducted with consumers on a credit basis.   Each of the three national credit reporting agencies (Trans Union, Equifax, and Experian) and affiliate credit bureaus serviced by their networks, as well as remaining locally owned an operated credit bureaus, have consumer relations departments who are trained and certified to assist the consumer public in understanding the information contained in their credit report.  If you have been denied credit within the past 60 days you are entitled to a free disclosure from the reporting bureau.  Otherwise you are able to obtain the disclosure for a small fee.   No one, including a credit repair organization, can represent that accurate information can be removed from your credit report, regardless of whether or not you pay a fee.  Information reported about adverse credit experiences with you will automatically be deleted as they become obsolete under the FCRA.   Only the passage of time and the prompt payment of your accounts can legally improve your credit history.

445045.title: Annuities
445045.description: An annuity is a contract between an individual and an issuer whereby the individual agree to give the issuer principal and in return the issuer guarantees fixed or variable payments over time. While annuities are not insurance policies, they are issued by insurance companies. An annuity is similar to a retirement plan in that you can fund it in a lump sum or a little at a time, and all capital in an annuity grows and compounds tax-deferred until you begin making withdrawals. Unlike retirement plans, however, there is no limit as to how much you can invest in annuities.

445040.title: Unclaimed Money
445040.description: This category contains sites to help people locate and recover unclaimed money.  This includes any type of site that provides useful information to locate and recover unclaimed money, such as: government, non-profit and commercial services, guides, advice, directories and tips.  This category is international and is meant to be helpful to people around the world.  The term "unclaimed money" is used here, but other terms are also widely used (such as abandoned property, unclaimed assets or funds or accounts) and may appear in the category entries.  The definition of "unclaimed money" varies by jurisdiction.  Generally speaking, "unclaimed money" refers to any property or money has been inactive for a certain period.  This can include things like old savings accounts, checks, refunds, real estate, refunds, dividends, life insurance etc.  After it is declared unclaimed, it is turned over to a government agency for safekeeping until the owner returns to claim it.  Governments do not generally try to locate the owners of unclaimed money but do often provide free searching tools online.  Organizations also provide searching services to locate unclaimed money, as well as services to help you recovery the money.
